sections.html:
The Catawba County Tax Office lists, appraises and assesses all real and personal property in the county, and it collects the county's taxes. Call (828) 465-8414 with general questions and (828) 465-8436 to book a tax relief appointment. Relief applications can be mailed to Assessor's Office, Attn: Tax Relief, Box 368, Newton, NC 28658-0368.

The office has earned the Certificate of Excellence in Assessment Administration from the International Association of Assessing Officers. Your own bill depends on the parcel's value, the county rate, and the fire district or town where the parcel sits.

sections.h2: County, town and fire district rates
sections.html:
The county rate is .3985 per $100 of assessed value, and every parcel also pays either a fire district tax or a municipal tax. The county tax page prints the full list. Main figures are below.

Fire districts run from .061 for Oxford to .13 for Claremont Rural. Others include Cooksville at .0785, Propst at .072, Mtn View at .0855, Maiden Rural at .0983, Sherrills Ford/Terrell at .099, Conover Rural and Long View Rural at .10, Bandys at .1050, Catawba Rural at .117, Newton Rural at .121, St Stephens at .124 and Hickory Rural at .125.

A parcel inside a town or city pays that municipality's rate. A parcel outside pays the fire district rate that covers it. Check your bill or ask the tax office which applies, then add it to the county rate for the combined figure.

Catawba County revalues every four years. Current values took effect January 1, 2023, and the next countywide revaluation takes effect January 1, 2027. State law requires one only every eight years, so the county moves twice as fast. Staff are studying sales and market trends for the 2027 round.

New appeals open after the 2027 notices go out, in January 2027. The path starts with an informal review and moves up only if that fails:

  • When value notices are mailed, ask the tax office how to request an informal review, and use the form that comes with the notice.
  • If that fails, take the case to the county board of equalization and review. Ask for a hearing in writing or in person before adjournment.
  • The state Property Tax Commission is the next stop, reached by written notice filed within 30 days after the board mails its ruling.

Revaluation updates values, not rates. The rate is set in the annual budget ordinance, usually finalized in June. An appeal can lower your value but cannot change the rate.

The county tax relief page lists four programs: the elderly or disabled homestead exclusion, the disabled veteran exclusion, the circuit breaker deferment, and the AV-10 application for other exclusions. An owner may pick only one of the first three.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: for owners who were 65 or disabled on January 1, own the home, live in the county and report income under the printed limit. The formula takes off $25,000 or half the appraised value, whichever is greater. A 65-plus applicant skips the disability certificate, and approval carries forward until you move, sell, rent, change the deed or go over the income limit.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: removes up to $45,000 of assessed value from the permanent residence, with no income test. The county wants discharge papers plus VA certification of permanent, total, service-connected disability, or proof of specially adapted housing benefits.
  • Circuit breaker deferment: holds the bill to 4 or 5 percent of income for owners who have lived in and owned the home five years or more. The deferred part is a lien, repayable with interest for the current year and three earlier ones once the property transfers.

June 1 is the yearly cutoff for all three, and the circuit breaker needs a new application every year. The AV-10 for religious, charitable, historic and similar exclusions is filed in January. The 2026 income limit is $38,800, with $58,200 as the 150 percent mark for the circuit breaker.

Sale proceeds clear whatever tax is open. A year's lien attaches on the January 1 listing date, and the bill falls due September 1. Every parcel pays county tax plus a fire or town levy, so a Hickory payoff will not match one for a house in a rural fire district.

No interest is charged through January 5. Then it runs at 2 percent for the rest of January and three-fourths of a percent per month beyond.

Circuit breaker owners get the surprise: transferring the property is a disqualifying event, so the deferred amounts become payable at the sale. Ask the tax office for a statement showing the current bill and any deferred balance.

Deed charges are handled at the Register of Deeds, a separate office, where the seller pays the state excise tax before the deed records. A practical order is to request the written tax statement first, then give it to your closing attorney, who builds the payoff into the settlement statement. In a cash sale there is no lender payoff to line up, but the tax balance is still paid at closing.

The county seat uses Newton addresses, and Hickory, Conover, Claremont, Maiden, Long View, Catawba and Brookford are the other municipalities on the tax page. The July 1, 2025 estimate is 170,172 residents, in 77,827 housing units.

Owners hold 72.2 percent of homes, and the 2020-2024 median home value is $241,600.

faqs.q: What is the Catawba County property tax rate?
faqs.a: The county rate is .3985 per $100. Each parcel adds either a fire district rate or a town or city rate (.46 in Hickory, .45 in Newton, for instance), and the two together make the combined rate.

faqs.q: When do Catawba County property values change next?
faqs.a: The next countywide revaluation takes effect January 1, 2027, after the one that took effect January 1, 2023. Catawba County revalues every four years, and appeals open once notices are mailed.

faqs.q: Which phone line handles Catawba County tax relief?
faqs.a: Call (828) 465-8436 to book a tax relief appointment, or (828) 465-8414 for general questions. Applications can be mailed to Assessor's Office, Attn: Tax Relief, Box 368, Newton, NC 28658-0368. The homestead deadline is June 1.

faqs.q: Do I have to pay off deferred circuit breaker taxes when I sell?
faqs.a: Yes. Selling ends the deferment, and the deferred amounts for this year and the three before it become payable with interest. Get the balance from the tax office before closing so it can be paid from the proceeds.

faqs.q: Is a disabled veteran exclusion available in Catawba County?
faqs.a: Yes. It excludes up to $45,000 of assessed value of a permanent residence and has no income limit. The veteran needs discharge proof plus VA certification of permanent and total service-connected disability, and the application is due by June 1.
